subject.title: External issue implementation intake queues work that the repair allowlist rejects

question: Should external hot targets remain review-only by default, or should maintainers define a narrowly approved external-repair allowlist that both intake and execution enforce?
rationale: The source boundary controls autonomous repair authority across repositories; choosing between rejecting external jobs and approving a limited execution scope is a policy decision, not a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Review-only external targets
options.body: Keep external repositories eligible for review but reject them before durable repair intake unless they are in the core execution scope.

options.title: Approved external repair scope
options.body: Define and document a narrow external repository allowlist, then make the same policy available to intake, job reconciliation, executor configuration, and CrabFleet registration.

recommendation.title: Review-only external targets
recommendation.body: Keep external repositories eligible for review but reject them before durable repair intake unless they are in the core execution scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged repair-dispatch history is the strongest available connection to the execution path affected by this authorization decision.
